These instantiations separate the cryptographic properties sufficient for randomness certification from the additional structure required for efficient verification within our commitment-based framework.

papers.title_en: More than a Lifetime: Towards Precision Predictions for $B$-Meson Decays in the Standard Model and Beyond
papers.abstract_en: This thesis investigates B-meson lifetimes as probes of Standard Model (SM) dynamics and physics beyond the SM (BSM), employing the Heavy Quark Expansion (HQE) and light-cone sum rules (LCSR). Within the HQE, we calculate at leading order in QCD the complete dimension-seven two-quark contributions to the CKM-favoured non-leptonic transitions $b\to c\bar{u}d$ and $b\to c\bar{c}s$, providing analytical Wilson coefficients for the $1/m_b^4$ corrections. We then extend the dimension-six Darwin contribution to a model-independent BSM framework, deriving the Wilson coefficients through order $1/m_b^3$ for a general non-leptonic effective Hamiltonian. We also determine the corresponding dimension-six four-quark weak annihilation contributions. As a special case, our results provide previously missing dimension-five and dimension-six contributions induced by SM QCD-penguin operators. Finally, we investigate B-mesogenesis, which connects the cosmic matter-antimatter asymmetry and dark matter to exotic B-meson decays. We study inclusive decay rates and lifetime ratios within the HQE and exclusive $B^+\to pψ$ decays using LCSR. Comparisons with experimental constraints from BaBar, Belle and Belle II restrict the allowed parameter space. We also identify kinematic regions where power-suppressed contributions exceed the leading terms, highlighting limitations of the HQE. Together, these studies advance the theoretical understanding of heavy-hadron lifetimes, strengthen the bridge between precision flavour physics and physics beyond the SM, and open new avenues for probing the interplay between heavy-quark dynamics and the dark sector.

papers.title_en: Characterization of integrating-sphere systematic effects for photon calibration of the KAGRA gravitational wave detector
papers.abstract_en: Photon calibration (Pcal) systems are essential for accurately reconstructing gravitational-wave strain in laser interferometric detectors. In the KAGRA Pcal system, the laser power applied to the end test mass is measured using integrating-sphere power sensors. During the first part of the fourth observing run (O4a), repeated calibration measurements showed scatter larger than expected from the uncertainties assigned to individual measurements. Although this excess scatter was empirically reflected in the previously reported calibration uncertainties, its physical origin was not identified. In this study, we experimentally characterize the response of the integrating spheres used in the KAGRA calibration chain with respect to three incident-beam conditions: incidence angle, polarization, and beam position. Based on these measurements and the reproducibility of the integrating-sphere placement in each calibration configuration, we evaluate the corresponding systematic uncertainties and explicitly incorporate them into the uncertainty model for the O4a Pcal-X calibration measurements. The inclusion of these previously unmodeled effects substantially improves the consistency between the estimated uncertainties and the observed scatter, particularly for calibration parameters measured at the KAGRA end station, where the reduced chi-square values decrease from values as large as $10^3$ to values of order unity to several. These results indicate that variations in the incident-beam conditions of integrating-sphere power sensors account for a substantial part of the previously unexplained scatter and establish a more physically motivated framework for evaluating Pcal laser-power calibration uncertainty. They also provide a basis for future reduction of the calibration uncertainty through improved control of the incident-beam conditions.

papers.title_en: Symmetry algebra of a charged harmonic oscillator in the field of the Dirac magnetic monopole
papers.abstract_en: A charged particle bound by an isotropic harmonic potential to a Dirac magnetic monopole, with the centrifugal term that makes the orbits close, has degeneracies beyond rotational invariance: for integer $q$, the product of the electric and magnetic charges, the levels are those of the oscillator with the states of angular momentum $l<|q|$ removed. The conserved rank-2 tensor $T$ built from the ladder operators that accounts for them was identified thirty-five years ago, but the algebra it generates with the angular momentum $\mathbf{J}$ was not obtained. We obtain its relations in covariant form and identify it. It is polynomial but not quadratic, and the shift $T'=T+2(H-1)J^{(2)}$ by the quadrupole of $\mathbf{J}$, and only this one, makes all commutators polynomials in $\mathbf{J}$. In each sector of fixed energy and $J_z$, $(\mathbf{J}^2,T'_{zz})$ generates a cubic algebra of Heun--Racah type whose parameters are symmetric, up to a scalar shift, in the magnetic charge and the magnetic quantum number. At $q=0$, $T$ is the algebraic Heun operator of the pair (Casimir of $\mathfrak{so}(3)$, quadrupole of $\mathfrak{su}(3)$): the symmetry algebra is the $\mathfrak{so}(3)$-covariant extension of a Heun--Racah algebra. We define it abstractly and classify its multiplicity-free finite-dimensional representations at the energies of the system: besides the levels, they include, for nonzero integer $q$, a second family carried by the states the monopole removes, the kernel of the Newman--Penrose operator. All relations are derived from the dynamical algebra of the ladder operators and hold for integer and half-integer charges alike.

papers.title_en: FTWeave: Composing Logical Execution, Real-Time Decoding, and Magic-State Supply in Tightly Integrated Quantum-Classical Systems
papers.abstract_en: Fault-tolerant quantum applications depend on both decoded measurement information and a continuing supply of magic states. While an operation waits for either, its logical data require protection that produces more syndrome data and decoding work. Architects must provision the quantum and classical parts of the machine together, before complete systems are available to measure. FTWeave is a system-level simulator for this architectural exploration. It accepts OpenQASM 2/3 circuits, CUDA-Q Logical compiler artifacts, Stim circuits, and provider-derived physical inputs through adapters that preserve operation and measurement dependencies. Users bind these inputs to quantum resources, classical processors, memory, communication, and factory configurations. One event timeline determines application progress, resource ownership, and continuing protection. This supplies the system model needed to connect circuit and decoder evidence to application performance. Controlled demand studies and complete multiplier and Ising circuits show why the coupling changes provisioning decisions. A fixed-work approximation predicts a 3.55x multiplier speedup from additional factories where the coupled model gives almost none. Explicit ownership also changes useful capacity: increasing decoder workers alone has no benefit in a storage-constrained case, while increasing workers and feedback entries together gives 4.93x speedup. Selected color and hypergraph-product code mappings take 53-90% longer under decoder service variability, despite an unchanged mean. These comparisons identify useful resource combinations and distinguish protection work from the elapsed lifetime of quantum data.

papers.title_en: Prototype-Guided Optimization of Quantum Data Embeddings with Linear Cost
papers.abstract_en: In supervised quantum machine learning with classical data, classification performance critically depends on the geometry induced by quantum data embedding. Existing data-adaptive approaches rely on pairwise fidelity evaluations between samples, which scale as $O(B^2)$ for $B$ samples and create a computational bottleneck in iterative embedding optimization. To address this issue, we propose a prototype-guided framework for efficient data-adaptive quantum embedding. Using class-prototype separation and sample-to-prototype compactness, we derive a measurable lower certificate for class-ensemble distinguishability and construct a prototype-based objective requiring only $O(B)$ fidelity evaluations. We integrate this objective into an end-to-end pipeline that combines task-specific quantum circuit architecture optimization with continuous refinement of the data-embedding parameters. Across five benchmark datasets with up to 20 qubits, our method retains competitive quantum kernel support vector machine (SVM) performance while reducing fidelity-evaluation cost, with particularly strong gains over budget-matched pairwise optimization on T-MNIST. Geometric analyses examine how the learned embeddings relate to kernel alignment and classification margins, revealing dataset-dependent benefits and limitations. We further derive a prototype-based classifier in the reproducing kernel Hilbert space that provides an explicit witness for the SVM objective and a low-cost proxy for model selection, and extend the framework to multiple prototypes for multimodal class structures.

papers.title_en: Margin-Based Generalization for Quantum Machine Learning with Classical Data Encoding
papers.abstract_en: Understanding generalization is essential for assessing the practical viability of quantum machine learning. In many applications, quantum models operate on classical data that must first be encoded into quantum states, making the encoding part of the effective hypothesis class. We develop a margin-based generalization framework for this setting, covering both fixed and trainable quantum data encodings. For fixed encodings, the existing margin bound transfers unchanged. For trainable encodings, we derive a bound using a two-scale covering argument that combines the original margin-dependent term with an additive encoding-capacity term of order $\tilde O(\sqrt{L/m})$, where $L$ is the number of trainable encoding parameters and $m$ is the training-sample size. Across 19,440 simulated training runs spanning various image datasets, circuit architectures, and optimization settings, the inverse margin performs best among five baseline and two bound-derived complexity measures under conditional-independence and 90th-percentile sign-error criteria, within bootstrap uncertainty. These results provide a unified margin-based view of generalization in quantum machine learning with classical data.

papers.title_en: Exact Quantum Query Complexity of the Five-Bit Symmetric Boolean Function $\Exact^5_{3,4}$
papers.abstract_en: Let \(f = \text{EXACT}^5_{3,4}\) be the Boolean function that equals 1 exactly on inputs of Hamming weight 3 or 4. Earlier numerical studies reported success probabilities close to one using three queries, but the existence of an exact three-query algorithm had remained unresolved. This paper settles this problem by proving that the exact quantum query complexity of \(f\) is \(4\). For the lower bound, we express every three-query algorithm through layer-by-layer Gram matrices of low-degree Fourier coefficients. We then construct a fixed rational dual certificate whose slack matrices are all positive definite. This certificate separates the necessary Gram-matrix region from the exact-output condition and therefore rules out every exact algorithm using at most three queries in the stated model. The positivity verification reduces to five small rational matrices and Sylvester's criterion. For the upper bound, we invoke the previously known four-query algorithm for the seven-bit function \(\text{EXACT}^7_{3,4}\) and apply the standard padding reduction. To quantify the near-exact behavior, we use the same certificate to derive a valid, though not claimed tight, lower bound \(\frac{25600}{43779488192449}>0\) on the worst-case error of every algorithm using at most three queries. This positive error gap is compatible with the near-unit success probabilities reported in earlier numerical studies, which do not establish exact computation.

papers.title_en: BQP^cc is not contained in MA^cc
papers.abstract_en: We exhibit a bipartite language with a poly-logarithmic quantum communication protocol and polynomial Merlin-Arthur communication complexity.

papers.title_en: Comment on "The polarization hierarchy for polynomial optimization over convex bodies, with applications to nonnegative matrix rank"
papers.abstract_en: We revisit the feasibility and convergence claims for the polarization hierarchy of Plávala, Ligthart and Gross [Linear Algebra Appl. 723 (2025) 15--32]. Counterexamples show that the stated assumption is insufficient for the feasibility characterization and for convergence of the hierarchy with the polarization constraint. We establish corrected results under a stronger algebraic condition and supply a missing compactness argument.

papers.title_en: PRIMA prototype spaceflight KID readout electronics laboratory characterization
papers.abstract_en: We present further development and testing of prototype kinetic inductance detector (KID) readout electronics for the PRobe far-Infrared Mission for Astrophysics (PRIMA). PRIMA is a NASA Probe-class astrophysics mission concept with two science instruments, FIRESS and PRIMAger, which provide spectroscopic and polarimetric imaging from 24 to 261 um. Together these instruments will explore the far-infrared sky with spatial-spectral mapping speeds that exceed previous studies by orders of magnitude, opening a vast discovery space. This increase in mapping speed is achieved by densely packed ultra-sensitive KIDs and cryogenically cooled optics. The PRIMA flight readout electronics will use the build-to-print SpaceCube Mini v3.0 which houses a radiation-tolerant Kintex KU060 field programmable gate array (FPGA). A custom high-speed digitizer board is being designed along with an RF electronics (RFE) board. The RFE was designed to provide programmable gain, band filtering, and RF switching between instruments. The prototype readout electronics, including the RFE, use functionally equivalent parts to the flight parts. In this proceeding we measure the readout loopback noise performance in the second Nyquist zone and timestream cross-talk performance. We present preliminary sweeps with the prototype readout coupled to prototype FIRESS detectors. Lastly, we demonstrate a cosmic ray pulse detection and real-time removal with an algorithm implemented in firmware.
publication_info: 13, Proc. SPIE 14156, Millimeter, Submillimeter, and Far-Infrared Detectors and Instrumentation for Astronomy XIII, 141560Y (20 Aug 2026), 141560, publication, Astronomy

papers.title_en: Ergotropy of nonequilibrium steady states beyond the full secular approximation
papers.abstract_en: Understanding the generation and activation of ergotropy, the maximum work extractable by cyclic unitary operations, is central to quantum battery research. Positive-temperature thermal states are passive, whereas nonequilibrium environments can sustain nonpassive steady states with nonzero ergotropy. However, the full secular approximation commonly used in Lindblad descriptions can suppress steady-state coherence and obscure its contribution to ergotropy. Using a Bloch-Redfield master equation beyond the full secular approximation, we investigate the ergotropy of the nonequilibrium steady state (NESS) of two exchange-coupled qubits connected to independent thermal reservoirs. The NESS ergotropy of two qubits with the same frequency is entirely coherent and grows quadratically with temperature bias near equilibrium. In contrast, detuned qubits can exhibit incoherent ergotropy. We derive an exact analytical criterion for its activation and show that activation requires the hotter reservoir to be coupled to the qubit with the higher bare frequency. Comparing NESSs obtained with and without full secularization reveals quantitative and qualitative differences in ergotropy that reflect changes in both its coherent and incoherent contributions. The results clarify the mechanisms of NESS ergotropy activation and demonstrate the importance of retaining steady-state coherence beyond the full secular approximation when characterizing stationary work resources.

papers.title_en: Quantum-Classical Iterative Refinement for the Pressure-Poisson Equation on NISQ Hardware
papers.abstract_en: We present a hybrid quantum-classical iterative refinement for the pressure-Poisson equation of the incompressible Navier-Stokes projection method on noisy quantum hardware. Rather than solving the pressure equation once per time step, we solve it repeatedly for the normalized residual and scale each quantum direction by a least-squares fit to the physical residual. As a result, the error of the quantum solve enters as a contraction factor $\sinθ_k$ of the residual rather than as an error floor. This removes the requirement of a state infidelity below $10^{-7}$ that was estimated for single-solve schemes. The hardware noise then sets the rate of convergence but not the attainable accuracy, and it is this change of the role of the quantum solve, not an improvement of the hardware, that allows the residual to converge. With a boundary-consistent staggered (MAC) discretization, the pressure residual equals the velocity divergence left after projection up to the factor $Δt/ρ$. On the IBM processor ibm_cleveland, a four-qubit ($16\times16$) problem reached a relative residual below $10^{-7}$ within eight to ten corrections in all 20 runs of a pre-registered experiment, whereas a single solve with a comparable number of shots stopped at 0.33-0.59. In a six-qubit ($64\times64$) pilot, all three runs reached the same tolerance in 13 corrections. On the IonQ Forte processor, a manufactured-solution benchmark reached $5.6\times10^{-8}$ in nine corrections. With the variational training itself carried out on ibm_cleveland, the residual fell to $5.6\times10^{-4}$ in seven corrections, below the pre-specified tolerance of $10^{-3}$, at the rate predicted by a noise model. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first converged pressure solutions obtained on quantum hardware.

papers.title_en: Collective Strong Quantum Mpemba Effect in Accelerated Quantum Detectors
papers.abstract_en: Collective coupling to the Minkowski vacuum allows uniformly accelerated quantum detectors to exhibit a strong quantum Mpemba effect, in which a state initially farther from equilibrium relaxes faster than a closer one. We establish the existence of this effect for every fixed finite number of detectors $N\geq 2$ at sufficiently small transverse separation within the pointlike secular master equation. The mechanism originates from two reflection sectors whose populations are conserved by the leading collective dynamics. Weak intersector transfer at finite separation generates an isolated, parametrically slow relaxation mode. A simple family of initial states permits its leading-order cancellation by matching the equilibrium sector populations, while a corrected preparation eliminates the slow-mode amplitude exactly. We construct a reference state that establishes a genuine reversal of trace-distance ordering. Numerical calculations and local-rate-preserving controls identify the collective origin of the effect, while spatially smeared detector calculations support its persistence within the second-order secular framework. The same mechanism extends to detectors coupled to a common thermal field, with analytically distinct slow relaxation rates. Thus, strong Mpemba relaxation is not exclusive to acceleration but emerges from a more general interplay between collective dissipation, reflection-sector conservation, and weak symmetry-breaking transfer.

papers.title_en: Tensor-polarized gluon distribution {h1TTg} in the deuteron: QCD evolution and Drell-Yan phenomenology
papers.abstract_en: We study the QCD evolution of the tensor-polarized double-helicity-flip gluon distribution $h_{1TT}^g$ in the deuteron and its impact on proton-deuteron Drell-Yan production. The nonperturbative input is taken from the spin-1 spectator model and evolved at leading order with the autonomous gluon evolution equation. The uncertainty of the model fit is propagated to the tensor-polarized cross-section difference and the asymmetry $A_{E_{xy}}$ using an ensemble of 100 replicas. Compared with the earlier benchmark estimate based on a longitudinally polarized gluon distribution, the evolved spectator-model input gives smaller cross sections in most of the kinematic region and a much stronger decrease of $|A_{E_{xy}}|$ with $Q^2$. At sufficiently large center-of-mass energy, the asymmetry varies only slowly with $\sqrt{s}$, whereas the low-$\sqrt{s}$ and large-$Q^2$ regions probe the poorly constrained large-$x$ tail of the model. We also evolve the tensor-polarized gluon distribution $f_{1LL}^g$ in the coupled singlet-gluon system and assess its contribution to the reference cross-section sum. Its effect remains moderate in the kinematic region where the spectator-model prediction is under reasonable control.

papers.title_en: Logical-Space Theory of Ordered-Statistics Decoding for Quantum LDPC Codes
papers.abstract_en: Quantum decoding succeeds when a correction matches the logical class of the error, whereas ordered-statistics decoding (OSD) searches a finite list of physical corrections. We connect these spaces through a rank-$k$ logical-signature map $M_{\rm log}:\mathbb F_2^q\to\mathbb F_2^k$. For fixed, error-independent orderings it yields the exact logical-signature distribution, the OSD-0 logical error rate, and the logical-class coverage of any fixed list. For minimum-cost list decoding we prove $P_L=P_{\rm miss}+P_{\rm sel}$, separating absent-class from wrong-selection failures. Hypergraph-product and bivariate-bicycle codes are consistent with the coverage predictions. On the $[\![144,12,12]\!]$ gross code, 672 coverage-aware candidates outperform 899 combination-sweep candidates (paired McNemar $p=0.013$), while two lists with identical logical coverage give $P_L=11.30\%$ and $3.78\%$; the signature-based coverage compression persists across 30 random column orderings. Logical coverage and within-class representative selection are therefore complementary resources that candidate count alone does not capture. The framework guides OSD list construction and compression by identifying coverage requirements and distinguishing coverage losses from failures of representative selection.

papers.title_en: ECC3: a global model for evaporation residue cross sections in the synthesis of superheavy nuclei
papers.abstract_en: We present ECC3, an efficient model for evaporation residue (ER) cross sections in heavy-ion fusion reactions from light systems to superheavy-element synthesis. The ER cross section is factorized into capture, described by the universal empirical coupled channel (ECC2) model; compound-nucleus formation, given by the Zagrebaev-Greiner empirical Fermi function of the charge product; and survival against fission, obtained from a simplified HIVAP-type statistical-decay cascade. The capture sector is inherited unchanged from ECC2 and reproduces 348 measured capture excitation functions with a logarithmic RMSD of 0.29. A single set of model parameters for the formation and survival of compound nuclei is fitted to 60 measured ER excitation functions with the corresponding RMSD of 0.27. About 95% of both the capture and ER systems are reproduced within a factor of four. Because the fitted parameters are constrained by light, medium-mass and superheavy systems rather than anchored to the measured superheavy region, extrapolation to unmeasured reactions is well controlled. The model also resolves the individual $xn$ channels. It reproduces the measured $3n$--$5n$ excitation functions of $^{19}$F+$^{188}$Os and the systematic charge dependence of the maximal channel cross section for $^{48}$Ca-, $^{50}$Ti- and $^{54}$Cr-induced reactions. For the three element-119 reactions $^{50}$Ti+$^{249}$Bk, $^{54}$Cr+$^{243}$Am and $^{51}$V+$^{248}$Cm, it predicts $4n$ dominance, with maximum cross sections of 13.2 fb, 2.64 fb and 1.56 fb, respectively.

papers.title_en: Ultra-relativistic freeze-out of fermion dark matter through a heavy scalar mediator
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the production of Majorana fermion dark matter (DM) via a heavy scalar mediator during reheating, with particular emphasis on ultra-relativistic freeze-out (UFO). Depending on the mediator mass, interaction strengths, and reheating temperature, we identify three distinct production regimes: freeze-in, WIMP-like freeze-out, and UFO, all of which can account for the observed DM relic abundance. In the UFO regime, significant DM production can persist after chemical decoupling, while entropy injection during reheating simultaneously dilutes the DM yield. An accurate determination of the final relic abundance therefore requires a consistent treatment of both continued production and entropy dilution. We further examine the impact of scalar cubic interactions and find that they modify the boundaries between the different production regimes and reshape the relic-density contours. In particular, the results are more sensitive to the cubic coupling involving the mediator and the light scalar than to the heavy-scalar self-coupling.

papers.title_en: EntangledEdge: A Distributed System for Orbital Quantum Sensing and Learning
papers.abstract_en: An orbital quantum sensor is more precise than classical and holds its information in a quantum state's superposition and entanglement, which classical measurement collapses. Learning on quantum-sensed data therefore requires a distributed system in which the data stay quantum from sensor to inference. We present EntangledEdge, the first system architecture to unify orbital quantum sensing and learning end-to-end, with a quantum data plane and a classical control plane. It routes each event to a channel-matched model in a capacity-diverse bank, adapts its detection threshold without labels, and aggregates across stations by hardware fidelity. Evaluated with a hybrid prototype (real quantum processors, simulated orbit-to-ground link) over satellite telemetry, EntangledEdge achieves high-quality inference at bounded per-event cost, improves quantum processor utilization, and scales with fleet size.

papers.title_en: Phenomenology of Spontaneous CP-violation in 2HDMs
papers.abstract_en: Spontaneous CP violation (SCPV) provides an attractive possibility for explaining the origin of CP violation and the observed CP-violating phenomena in the quark sector. We investigate SCPV in the two-Higgs-doublet model as one of its simplest realizations, in which the additional Higgs bosons are necessarily non-decoupling and flavor misalignment in the Yukawa sector is required. The non-decoupling Higgs sector predicts sizable deviations from the Standard Model predictions even in the Higgs alignment limit: the decay rates of the discovered Higgs boson into $γγ$ and $Zγ$ can deviate by at least about $-10\%$ and $-4\%$, respectively, while the trilinear Higgs self-coupling can receive $\mathcal{O}(100)\%$ corrections. We consider a scenario in which the down-type quark and charged-lepton Yukawa matrices are flavor aligned, while flavor-violating interactions are allowed in the up-type quark sector to reproduce the Kobayashi-Maskawa phase. We explore the viable parameter space by imposing theoretical constraints together with experimental constraints from electroweak precision observables, flavor measurements, electric dipole moments, and LHC data. We find that a sizable flavor-violating top-charm Yukawa coupling remains allowed, giving rise to distinctive LHC signatures, including same-sign top-quark and three-top production as well as scalar cascade decays. We also find that the deviation in the trilinear Higgs self-coupling is correlated with the decay patterns of the additional neutral Higgs bosons, providing a connection between precision Higgs measurements and direct searches for the additional Higgs bosons. Our results demonstrate the importance of combining searches for additional Higgs bosons with precision Higgs measurements, complemented by flavor and electric-dipole-moment experiments, to probe SCPV.

papers.title_en: Probing dark-matter scenarios of Belle II excess in $B^+\to K^+M_X$ with $K^+\to π^+ M_X$ decays
papers.abstract_en: The hypothesis of top-philic dark matter as the origin of the Belle II excess events in $B\to K M_X$ decays has direct impact on $K\to πM_X$ decays: Both of these decays proceed via loop diagrams~with a top quark emitting some mediator field $R$ and the subsequent decay of $R$ into a pair of dark-matter fermions $\barχχ$. The Belle II results on $B\to K M_X$ allowed us to extract the parameters of the mediator $R$ with reasonable accuracy, whereas the sensitivity to the fermion mass $m_χ$ proved to be rather low. In contrast to $B\to K M_X$ decays, the $K\to πM_X$ decays exhibit a strong sensitivity to $m_χ$; therefore, if - upon reducing theoretical and experimental uncertainties - the tension between standard-model predictions for the $K\toπM_X$ decays and the most recent NA62 measurements becomes pronounced the latter decays may either enable the extraction of the value of $m_χ$ or provide a lower limit on~$m_χ$.

papers.title_en: Concatenated continuous-drive protection of exchange-based spin-qubit gates
papers.abstract_en: Exchange-based two-qubit gates in semiconductor spin qubits are sensitive to low-frequency detuning noise and control errors. Here, we extend concatenated continuous driving (CCD), implemented by phase modulation of a global microwave drive, to exchange-based SWAP and $\sqrt{\mathrm{SWAP}}$ operations between double-dressed spin qubits and investigate its effectiveness for protecting two-qubit gates. We find that CCD retains strong protection against quasistatic common-mode detuning errors while substantially improving robustness against Rabi-frequency errors and qubit-to-qubit Rabi-frequency mismatch compared with conventional continuous dressing. By contrast, the gate fidelity is impacted by differential detuning errors. By modeling partially correlated quasistatic detuning noise, we further show that the noise-averaged gate fidelity depends strongly on the spatial correlation of the qubit-frequency fluctuations, with positive correlations enhancing CCD protection by suppressing the differential-noise component. These results identify the symmetry and spatial correlation of qubit-frequency noise as key factors governing continuous-drive protection in coupled spin-qubit systems.

papers.title_en: Extraction of All Partial-Wave Interaction Parameters via Femtoscopy: The Central-Force Case
papers.abstract_en: We present a universal femtoscopic method to extract the source size and central-force interaction parameters for arbitrary partial waves from experimental data, with the interaction parameters defined in the effective-range expansion. The method is based on the Wronskian determinant and is applicable to both the Coulomb and non-Coulomb cases. This approach is numerically verified against simulated neutron-neutron and proton-proton correlation data obtained from the Reid potential.

papers.title_en: Adiabatic controlled-$Z$ gate for neutral atoms with Förster-enhanced Rydberg dressing
papers.abstract_en: We study an adiabatic controlled-$Z$ (CZ) gate for neutral atoms in which dipole-dipole coupling between nearly degenerate Rydberg pair states enhances the interaction between dressed ground states. This coupling produces an avoided crossing in the two-atom dressed-state spectrum. Approaching the crossing enhances the dressed interaction, but also reduces the dressed-state gap and increases the Rydberg admixture. We identify a Förster-enhanced operating range in which the required conditional phase is accumulated with adiabatic return and small transient Rydberg population. We then analyze the finite-time dynamics of the two-qubit computational states under a smooth pulse. Reducing the dressing strength weakens the dressed interaction, so maintaining the target phase at the same pulse duration requires operation closer to the avoided crossing, where the Rydberg admixture increases. This dependence is then used to select the shortest gate at a fixed peak Rabi frequency in the Förster-enhanced operating range that accumulates the CZ phase with high Bell-state fidelity while keeping the Rydberg population small. Changing the Förster defect shifts the avoided crossing, while the gate parameters change only weakly. For a specific rubidium Förster channel, the selected gate corresponds to experimentally relevant laser coupling, pulse duration, and interatomic separation. We also estimate errors from the finite Rydberg lifetime and from weak excitation of a neighboring spectator atom. For the parameters considered, the spectator-induced error remains below the finite-lifetime contribution.

papers.title_en: Efficient Quantum Algorithm for Mixed-State Quantum Geometry
papers.abstract_en: Mixed-state quantum geometry plays a fundamental role in quantum metrology, multiparameter estimation, and the characterization of quantum many-body systems. Yet, unlike its pure-state counterpart, accessing mixed-state geometry requires solving an ill-conditioned Lyapunov equation for the symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD), posing a major challenge for resource-efficient quantum computation. Here we address the challenge and develop a novel quantum algorithmic framework for efficiently accessing the quantum Fisher information matrix (QFIM) and quantum geometric tensor (QGT) of mixed states. Our key insight is to uncover a previously unexplored connection between the positive semidefinite structure of density matrices and exponentially convergent Gauss-Laguerre quadrature, enabling an efficient integral-based construction of the SLD. A rigorous complexity analysis further establishes the resource efficiency of our algorithm, demonstrating logarithmic precision dependence and double-logarithmic ancillary-qubit overhead at fixed conditioning. Building on this construction, we achieve near-Heisenberg precision scaling for diagonal QFI estimation without quantum phase estimation and construct unified block encodings of the full QFIM and QGT under a bounded spectral-gap assumption. A complementary regularized algorithm extends efficient diagonal estimation to exponentially small spectral gaps under a bounded-response condition. Our results establish a resource-efficient route to coherent mixed-state quantum geometry, enabling its direct integration into quantum linear-algebra algorithms without classical reconstruction and opening new possibilities for quantum-enhanced multiparameter metrology.

papers.title_en: Forward $χ_c$ production in $pp$ and $pA$ collisions within the CGC+NRQCD framework
papers.abstract_en: We study the forward $χ_{cJ}$ production in the low $p_{\perp}$ region in proton-proton $(pp)$ and proton-nucleus $(pA)$ collisions at the LHC within the framework of non-relativistic QCD (NRQCD) factorization and the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) effective field theory. Incorporating the small-$x$ gluonic evolution via the running-coupling Balitsky-Kovchegov equation with various initial conditions, we systematically analyze the cross section ratio $R_{χ_{c}}=σ_{χ_{c2}}/σ_{χ_{c1}}$, and find that the theoretical predictions weakly depend on these inputs. Our predictions align well with the LHCb measurements for $p\mathrm{Pb}$ collisions, however, overshoot those for $pp$ collisions. We further investigate the feed down fractions $F_{χ_{c1,2}\to J/ψ}=σ_{χ_{c1,2}\to J/ψ}/σ_{J/ψ}$. We notice that with the experimental measurement of prompt $J/ψ$ cross section as inputs in the denominator the CGC+NRQCD predictions broadly match the data when choosing the standard McLerran-Venugopalan initial conditions. In contrast, implementing purely theoretical CGC+NRQCD predictions for both $J/ψ$ and $χ_{c}$ production yield systematic discrepancies across all tested parameters. This highlights a persistent challenge in achieving a simultaneous, unified description of $χ_{c}$ and prompt $J/ψ$ production within the current framework.

papers.title_en: Low-Field J-Coupling Spectroscopy Measured with a Diamond Nitrogen Vacancy Spectrometer
papers.abstract_en: Nitrogen vacancy centers in diamond (NVs) are point defects well suited to quantum sensing of magnetic fields. NV spin states can be initialized and read out optically with high spatial resolution, enabling detection of pL-scale volumes of nuclear spins. Using Coherently Averaged Synchronized Readout (CASR), standard NMR spectroscopy techniques such as free decay, spin echo, and PGSE have been performed with Hz-scale spectral resolution using NV-diamond sensors. However, using NV detection for conventional high-resolution NMR at multi-tesla fields is challenging due to the need to manipulate NV electronic spins at resonance frequencies 100 GHz or higher. Low-field J-coupling spectroscopy provides an alternative path to chemical resolution in a regime more easily accessible to NVs. Here, we demonstrate homonuclear and heteronuclear J-coupling spectroscopy using an NV-NMR spectrometer based on permanent magnets operating at $\sim$890 kHz proton Larmor frequency (bias magnetic field $\sim$21 mT). This field strength enables chemical characterization based on J-coupling using sequences such as Synchronized Echo (SyncE) and Spin-Echo Double Resonance (SEDOR), which do not require the strong chemical shift dispersion and pristine field homogeneity of high-field NMR. The frequency range is easily detected by NVs using standard XY dynamical decoupling sequences and is well-suited for applying Overhauser DNP, which can boost proton signal by two orders of magnitude. We acquire initial NV-NMR measurements of T$_1$, T$_2$, and Overhauser DNP in glycerol before advancing to SEDOR spectroscopy of methanol-$^{13}$C and a methanol-$^{13}$C/acetonitrile-2-$^{13}$C mixture at sample volumes $\sim$50 pL, in which we demonstrate measurement of $^1J_\text{CH}$ couplings and resolution between species. We also acquire a homonuclear J-coupling spectrum of a natural-abundance propylene carbonate sample.

papers.title_en: A 4-20 GHz Superconducting 90deg Hybrid Using Capacitively Loaded Coupled Lines for 2SB Heterodyne Receivers
papers.abstract_en: We report the design and cryogenic characterisation of a broadband superconducting 90deg intermediate-frequency (IF) hybrid covering 4 to 20 GHz for sideband-separating (2SB) heterodyne receivers. The hybrid is implemented in thin-film niobium using capacitively loaded edge coupled transmission lines, avoiding the air-bridge interconnections required in Lange-coupler layouts while retaining a compact superconducting implementation with low loss and good quadrature balance. Cryogenic measurements using Vector Network Analyser (VNA) show amplitude and phase imbalance better than 0.6 dB and 6deg, respectively, across the full band. When used in a 2SB receiver, this level of IF balance is consistent with the observed image-rejection performance in the 10-20 dB range, for the full receiver. The design supports the development of wide-instantaneous-bandwidth 2SB receivers for millimeter and submillimeter observatories, improving spectral grasp for broadband line surveys and high-redshift line searches.

papers.title_en: Global analyses of PDFs in the precision era
papers.abstract_en: Parton distribution functions or PDFs are determined through global fits to an ever-increasing array of data, including deep-inelastic scattering at fixed-target experiments and HERA, and hadron collisions at the Tevatron and LHC. As the dataset has expanded, theoretical accuracy has improved from partial next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) coverage about 20 years ago to approximate N$^3$LO global fits today. The fitting collaborations must reconcile these complex calculations and data analyses while ensuring that quoted PDF uncertainty bands remain reliable.

papers.title_en: Characterizing Local and Correlated Pauli Noise in Quantum Teleportation Circuits
papers.abstract_en: We analytically characterize how the location and the local or correlated structure of stochastic Pauli errors affect a three-qubit coherent quantum-teleportation circuit. Independent local channels and a fully correlated two-qubit channel are inserted separately in six configurations. Propagating each Pauli-error realization through the Clifford circuit yields the effective channel on Bob's qubit and analytical expressions for the average and state-resolved fidelities. Under a common ordered-pair probability convention, the six configurations form three pairs that induce equivalent reduced channels on Bob. Within each pair, corresponding Pauli-error realizations have the same probabilities and produce the same effective Pauli operator on Bob's output state. The equivalence therefore holds for every input state within the stochastic Pauli models considered here, rather than only for the average fidelity. Correlated Z errors do not affect the output for the first pair; local X and Z errors exhibit complementary qubit sensitivity for the second; and correlated same-axis Pauli errors cancel for the third. These results classify the error response of the selected circuit configurations and show that it depends jointly on the error statistics, Pauli axis, and position within the protocol.

papers.title_en: Common origin of the Belle-BESIII line-shape difference of $Λ_c^+\barΛ_c^-$, $D_s D_{s1}$ and $D_s D_{s2}^*$ from $e^+ e^-$ annihilation
papers.abstract_en: The longstanding Belle--BESIII discrepancies in the $e^+e^-\toΛ_c^+\barΛ_c^-$, $D_sD_{s1}(2536)$, and $D_sD_{s2}^{*}(2573)$ line shapes remain an unresolved puzzle, with enhancements observed by Belle that are absent or much weaker in the BESIII measurements. In this work, we propose a new mechanism based on the radiative production of higher charmonia to explain these differences. Such processes may contribute to Belle's initial-state radiation samples, and the luminosity normalization increases their contribution to the extracted cross sections. With the vector contributions scaled by BESIII data, a pseudoscalar charmonium $η_c(6S)$ contribution can describe the baryonic enhancement, while an introduced $χ_{c2}(5P)$ contribution can describe the enhancements in both meson channels. This mechanism offers a possible common explanation for these differences and, as a bonus, suggests a way to search for missing higher charmonia at Belle II.

papers.title_en: Light meson decays at BESIII
papers.abstract_en: The world's largest sample of $J/ψ$ events accumulated with the BESIII detector offers a unique opportunity to investigate $η$ and $η'$ physics via the radiative transition processes $J/ψ\to γη/η'$. A selection of recent highlights in light meson spectroscopy achieved at BESIII is reviewed in these proceedings, including evidence for the cusp effect in $η' \to π^0π^0η$, precision studies of the decay mechanisms of $η\to 3π$ and $η' \to 4π$, electromagnetic transition form factor measurements with $η/η' \to γe^+e^-$ and $η' \to π^+π^-l^+l^-$, as well as searches for rare decays of $η$ and $η'$ into lepton pairs, including $η\to l^+l^-$ and $η/η' \to l^+l^-l^+l^-$~($l = e, μ$).

papers.title_en: One-loop mixing matrix of the N=1 SYM Supercurrent operator upon renormalization on the Lattice using stout-smeared Links
papers.abstract_en: We extend the perturbative investigation of the renormalization and mixing patterns of the supercurrent operator in lattice ${\cal N}=1$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills (SYM) theory, using stout-smeared gauge links. We employ the SLiNC action for gluinos and a family of Symanzik improved gauge actions for gluons. Building upon previous studies employing clover-improved fermions and the Wilson gauge action, we compute the one-loop mixing matrix of the supercurrent operator among gauge-invariant and gauge-variant operators. Particular emphasis is placed on the structure of operator mixing in the presence of stout smearing parameters. Our results contribute toward refining fine-tuning strategies necessary for the restoration of supersymmetry in the continuum limit, and provide a stepping stone for future perturbative and nonperturbative investigations in supersymmetric theories on the lattice.

papers.title_en: Quantum-Correlation-Based Multi-Emitter Localization in Information-Limited Regimes via Learned Inference
papers.abstract_en: Quantum correlation measurements have emerged as a powerful tool for localizing multiple emitters with subwavelength separation. Multi-emitter localization consists of two distinct tasks: identifying the emitter count $N$ and estimating their positions $\left\{x^{i}\right\}$. Existing fit-and-select frameworks fit the measured intensity and autocorrelation data using several models corresponding to different values of $N$ and then select the best-supported model. This procedure lets errors from the multi-parameter optimization of emitter positions propagate into the choice of model, degrading performance under photon-limited and high-background conditions. We propose a method that directly infers the emitter count and positions from the multimodal data via learned inference. Learned inference improves both the emitter-counting accuracy and localization precision compared to the fit-and-select method. It achieves more than tenfold improvement in precision and requires up to five times fewer photons to achieve practically meaningful localization with the largest gains observed under low photon counts, strong background, narrowly spaced emitter configurations, and spatially truncated data. This photon-efficient quantum-assisted localization framework offers a promising route toward real-time biological imaging and single-particle tracking in densely labeled samples.

papers.title_en: Scaling laws for contamination traversal times during vacuum breaks in superconducting accelerators
papers.abstract_en: A sudden loss of vacuum in a superconducting radio-frequency (SRF) accelerator drives warm gas into the evacuated beamline, where it propagates through interconnected SRF cavities cooled by liquid helium, causing surface contamination, intense heat deposition, and dangerous pressure buildup. Yet predicting how such a failure propagates through realistic multicell cavities has remained difficult because compressible gas dynamics, condensation and cryogenic heat transfer are strongly coupled. Here we develop and experimentally validate a multidimensional computational framework that resolves these processes, and apply it to a full-scale nine-cell SRF cavity. We find that the repeated cell geometry produces staircase-like gas-front propagation, as impingement, recirculation and localized cryopumping strongly retard the bulk flow within each cell. Across a broad range of breach sizes, the cavity traversal time follows a robust power-law scaling with leakage area, providing quantitative guidance for the response time of beamline isolation and protection systems. The simulations also reveal a geometry-confined Mach disk whose position and size track the advancing gas front, suggesting that its acoustic emission could potentially enable rapid, non-invasive detection and localization of vacuum failures. These findings pave the way for a new generation of predictive diagnostics and protection strategies to safeguard large-scale superconducting accelerators.

papers.title_en: Local response theory of multiparameter sudden-quench quantum Otto engines
papers.abstract_en: Multiparameter quantum Otto engines raise an optimization problem absent in single-parameter cycles: which small quench vector maximizes the quadratic approximation to the exact output work in a multidimensional control space? We develop a local response theory for sudden-quench Otto engines with quantum working media described by linearly controlled Hamiltonians. We show that the local quadratic work decomposes into a thermal-bias gain and a quadratic response cost, whose competition determines the quench vector that maximizes the local quadratic work at a prescribed quench amplitude. We illustrate the theory in a minimal two-level working medium, where radial and transverse quenches play distinct roles, and in a finite interacting XYZ spin chain, where the resulting quench vector is determined by the balance between thermal-bias and response cost. Our results provide a practical local criterion for designing small multiparameter quenches in sudden-quench quantum Otto engines.

papers.title_en: Recent Advances in Transverse-Momentum--Dependent Distributions in Lattice QCD
papers.abstract_en: Unraveling the three-dimensional structure of hadrons is a central objective in modern nuclear and particle physics. Transverse Momentum Dependent parton distributions (TMDs) provide crucial insights into the interplay between partonic transverse motion and spin, and are indispensable for describing a wide range of high-energy processes at facilities such as JLab, COMPASS, the LHC, and the upcoming Electron-Ion Collider. In recent years, significant progress has been made in accessing TMDs from lattice QCD using novel approaches. Methods based on ratios of Mellin moments, large-momentum effective theory (LaMET), and Coulomb-gauge techniques have enabled first-principles investigations of the Collins-Soper kernel, intrinsic soft functions, TMD wave functions, and TMDPDFs. Recent lattice results for both unpolarized and spin-dependent distributions, including the Boer-Mulders function, demonstrate the feasibility of extracting transverse-momentum--dependent information directly from QCD. This paper reviews recent advances in lattice-QCD studies of TMDs, outlines remaining challenges such as continuum and infinite-momentum extrapolations, and discusses future directions toward precision determinations of hadron structure in three dimensions.

papers.title_en: SIESTA-QCOMP: Bridging Classical and Quantum Computing for Strongly Correlated Systems
papers.abstract_en: Density Functional Theory (DFT) is the established workhorse of computational materials science, yet it faces fundamental challenges with strongly correlated electrons, such as in transition metal complexes and bond-breaking processes. While quantum computing offers a theoretically exact path to resolve these problems, current hardware limitations prohibit fully quantum simulations of realistic material systems. To bridge this gap, we present SIESTA-QCOMP, a modular suite embedding quantum methodologies within DFT. Harnessing SIESTA's localised basis set, we implement a projection-based embedding scheme that treats the bulk environment classically while mapping the strongly correlated "impurity" subspace to a quantum processor. The architecture uses a socket-based driver to orchestrate workflows between the Fortran-based SIESTA engine and Python-based frameworks like Qiskit, ensuring high interoperability. We detail the hybrid workflow, currently utilising a Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE), and discuss the road map toward methods such as Sample-based Quantum Diagonalisation (SQD). We illustrate the framework on an hypothetical iron porphyrin calculation and argue that such hybrid architectures are not merely interim solutions but essential foundations for integrating quantum utility into materials design, as envisioned by our broader QCOMP4DFT initiative.

papers.title_en: ConQUESTA: Topology-Aware Post-Training Structural Pruning of Quantum Neural Networks
papers.abstract_en: Deploying quantum neural networks (QNNs) on sparse hardware requires preserving task accuracy while reducing compiler-induced two-qubit gates, SWAPs, and depth. We present ConQUESTA (\underline{C}onstrained \underline{Qu}antum \underline{E}ntangler \underline{S}election with \underline{T}opology \underline{A}wareness), a post training pruning framework that combines task saliency with compiler cost, screens candidate entanglers, and searches complete pruning masks under an explicit accuracy constraint. Unlike one-shot ranking, each mask is transpiled as a whole across multiple coupling topologies. Across 4-, 6-, and 8-qubit QNNs and eight model seeds at 55% pruning, ConQUESTA achieves mean resource reductions of 61.6% on Breast Cancer, 72.0% on Digits01, and 82.2% on Iris, exceeding the strongest matched simple baseline by 3.5, 1.7, and 8.9 percentage points, respectively. Fixed-mask recovery raises feasibility from 16/24 to 22/24 runs. In a fixed-k=4 scaling study on a scaling probe of 4 to 12-qubits, the raw mask space grew from 495 to 12.1M while the evaluated masks increase only from 189 to 305. Resource-weight changes alter depth/routing priorities with at most a 0.44-point mean validation shift.

papers.title_en: On the relationship between the POVM framework and the no-signaling hypothesis
papers.abstract_en: The quantum foundations literature contains dozens of "no-signaling" arguments that rely on the Born rule or, more generally, the positive operator-valued measure (POVM) framework to show that the resources of non-relativistic quantum mechanics (NRQM) cannot be used to send superluminal signals. What these arguments typically establish, however, is not a prohibition on superluminal signaling per se, but the seemingly stronger claim that signaling at any speed between mutually isolated systems is forbidden. This paper gives a precise formulation of this claim, the no-signaling hypothesis, and investigates the following converse question: under what additional assumptions does it imply that all experimental outcome probabilities are described by POVMs? Surprisingly few are needed: given the standard NRQM representation of composite experiments and two textbook claims about marginal probabilities, the no-signaling hypothesis is equivalent to the universality of the POVM framework. More broadly, by formalizing the relevant concepts and deriving the logical relationships between them, the paper shows that the no-signaling hypothesis can be used to derive most, though not all, of the probability-generating fragment of NRQM. The resulting map of implications clarifies which common postulates of NRQM are logically interrelated and which can be modified independently.

papers.title_en: Partially isophase electro-magnetic configurations
papers.abstract_en: Separation of variables in Schrödinger equation allows an infinite-dimensional family of physically distinct field configurations that are dynamically indistinguishable in one selected sector, labeled by a conserved quantum number, while differing in all others. We call such a symmetry a partial isophase symmetry. Two main examples are considered: axially symmetric magnetic backgrounds (a rigid spectral flow of the Fock--Darwin oscillator, purely magnetic isophase families, and a two-channel extension) and a Cartesian slab geometry (magnetic barriers in two-dimensional electron gases, treated in the Appendices). We further discuss the consequences of this symmetry for the inverse spectral problem and consider its quasiclassical counterpart.

papers.title_en: Cayley access models for matrix functions: reachable class and cost
papers.abstract_en: We study how to compute $f(A)b$ on a quantum computer, where $A$ is Hermitian. When $f$ is nonsmooth or has localized difficulty in the spectrum, classical numerical linear algebra approximates it with rational functions rather than polynomials. We propose the Cayley transform, parameterized by $σ\in \mathbb{R}$ and $γ> 0$, as an alternative to the standard quantum access model. The two parameters let one concentrate accuracy where $f$ is difficult, which standard models can achieve only by raising the polynomial degree globally. This transformation converts Hermitian matrices to unitaries, allowing generalized quantum signal processing to apply Laurent polynomials bounded on the unit circle. We compare three access models (block encoding, matrix exponential, and Cayley encoding) in terms of query complexity and of the cost of their circuit realization. When the difficulty of $f$ is localized in the spectrum, the Cayley encoding reduces the required degree by a factor of three to four, and it represents the shifted resolvent exactly at degree one. For spectral projectors, the standard models cannot reach the target accuracy at fixed degree, because their approximants cannot concentrate resolution near the discontinuity. Realizing the Cayley encoding from a block encoding requires solving a shifted linear system, whose cost offsets its query-complexity gain over the standard models. For structured matrices arising in practice, however, low-depth circuits for the encoding can be constructed directly, and the gain is preserved at the circuit level.

papers.title_en: Recursive Operator Localization and Spectral Gap Descent via the Geometry of Local Spectral Expansion
papers.abstract_en: We introduce Recursive Operator Localization (ROL), a framework for constructing hierarchies of local energy problems linked by linear maps between Hilbert spaces. To address spectral-gap problems, including those arising in quantum systems, we study a realization of ROL by nested subspaces indexed by a weighted simplicial complex. Using spectral gaps of auxiliary classical random walks on links, we propagate geometric estimates upward and use them to turn local spectral gaps at the bottom of the hierarchy into a spectral-gap bound for the global operator. For weighted scalar-valued functions on facets, the ROL decomposition becomes the law of total variance, recovering classical spectral-gap bounds from local link expansion (Alev and Lau, STOC 2020). Moreover, for positive binary spin distributions, conditional influence describes the overlap of the corresponding subspaces, yielding known heat-bath gap bounds from spectral independence (Anari, Liu, and Oveis Gharan, FOCS 2020). The framework also offers a route toward quantum Gibbs sampling, with applications requiring model-specific geometric estimates and energy comparisons.

papers.title_en: Improved aluminum film transport properties and enhanced TES response in athermal phonon detectors: implications for quasiparticle dynamics
papers.abstract_en: Our detectors for Dark Matter and Coherent Elastic Neutrino--Nucleus Scattering (CE$ν$NS) use photolithographically patterned superconducting athermal phonon sensors that are coupled to kg-scale absorbers of different materials (germanium, silicon, sapphire). Following a particle interaction, athermal phonons from the bulk absorber break Cooper pairs in a superconducting aluminum film that surrounds a tungsten Transition Edge Sensor (TES) in equilibrium through electrothermal feedback. This sensor design is called Quasiparticle-trap-assisted Electro-thermal-feedback Transition-edge-sensor (QET). The QET aluminum film that absorbs the athermal phonons is patterned into fins with lengths limited by the quasiparticle diffusion length in aluminum. Improving the quasiparticle diffusion length in the superconducting aluminum is an area of vigorous research to improve phonon collection efficiency and increase the signal strength for lower-threshold searches. We report significantly improved aluminum films that show systematically larger grain sizes and residual-resistivity ratio (RRR) compared to detectors we have fabricated in the past. The improved RRR and grain sizes were expected to improve the collected signal for a given energy. We report higher signal strength achieved in a detector in comparison to another detector in which all other fabrication parameters were kept identical except for the aluminum film deposition.

papers.title_en: Encodings and Node Architecture: Lessons from the Fault-Tolerant Distributed Transversal Fanout
papers.abstract_en: An encoding choice specifies the quantum error-correcting code used to encode logical qubits at a given node. Different encoding choices may differ in the number of physical qubits, the number of encoded logical qubits, the code distance, and the available fault-tolerant operations. We study different encodings for a distributed transversal fanout operation and look at its implications on node architecture. Our experiments suggest that an encoding with higher distance, even if requiring more ebits, can yield a lower logical error rate for distributed operations, and that ``upgrading'' an encoding prior to distributed operations and having a cache, as part of node architecture, for qubits can be useful for distributed operations.

papers.title_en: Chirality-resolved imaging of spin waves with a quantum spin
papers.abstract_en: Spin waves carry their propagation direction in the handedness of their circularly polarized stray field, a property inaccessible to scalar magnetometers. In the Damon-Eshbach surface wave of an in-plane magnetized film, the dipolar field above the film rotates with a handedness fixed by the direction of travel. The nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centre in diamond is an intrinsic polarization analyser: a right-handed field about the NV axis drives one spin transition, and a left-handed field drives the other, in both the ground and the excited state. Here, we exploit the two excited-state transitions, which lie inside the spin-wave band of yttrium iron garnet (YIG), as a pair of chirality channels and image Damon-Eshbach waves in both directions. Because reflection from an etched boundary reverses the handedness, the incident and reflected waves appear as two lines in one spectrum and are imaged separately. In the ground state, the same rule applies, and the selected field drives Rabi oscillations, a route to chirality-selective control of the NV spin by magnons. Reading the two channels gives the direction of a spin wave at one point, without a phase reference. This advances chirality-resolved quantum sensing and provides insight into chiral spin-wave dynamics.

papers.title_en: Leading-twist proton parton distribution amplitude from scalar and axial-vector diquark correlations
papers.abstract_en: We compute the leading-twist proton parton distribution amplitude (PDA) using algebraic representations of the nucleon Faddeev wave function inspired by perturbation-theory integral representations. The PDA is obtained from a light-front projection of the covariant quark--diquark Faddeev amplitude and analysed in terms of its scalar- and axial-vector-diquark components. We derive analytic expressions for the corresponding diquark distribution amplitudes and their contributions to the proton PDA. The resulting distribution is broad and concave, with its maximum $(x_1,x_2,x_3)\approx(0.55,0.20,0.25)$ displaced from the symmetric configuration $(1/3,1/3,1/3)$, which corresponds to the maximum of the perturbative-QCD asymptotic form. Scalar-diquark correlations generate a strong asymmetry in the longitudinal momentum distribution, whereas axial-vector correlations redistribute momentum among the valence quarks and significantly reduce this asymmetry. We calculate low-order Mellin moments and obtain a compact parametrisation of the proton PDA at the hadronic scale, $μ_0=0.51\,\mathrm{GeV}$. We then perform the leading-order QCD evolution of its normalized shape to $μ=2\,\mathrm{GeV}$, finding that evolution reduces the momentum asymmetry while preserving a clear imprint of the non-perturbative quark--diquark correlations. The results provide insight into the role of such correlations in shaping the proton light-front structure and furnish non-perturbative input for studies of hard exclusive baryonic processes.

papers.title_en: Concrete Functions in Private Simultaneous Quantum Messages: Quantum Advantages and Structural Limitations
papers.abstract_en: Private simultaneous quantum messages (PSQM) provide a minimal model of noninteractive secure multiparty quantum computation, yet their communication complexity for concrete functions remains poorly understood. We show that familiar total functions already exhibit both genuine quantum advantages and strong structural limitations. For three-party equality on $n$-bit inputs, which determines whether the players' $n$-bit strings are identical, we construct an entanglement-assisted protocol with asymptotic communication $(1.633\ldots)n$ qubits, whereas every perfectly correct protocol without prior entanglement requires at least $3n$ qubits. For three-bit majority, one shared GHZ state and one transmitted qubit per player suffice for perfect correctness and perfect privacy, reducing the communication from the optimal classical cost of six bits to three qubits. Three-bit AND behaves differently. No perfectly correct and perfectly private protocol exists when the players share an arbitrary three-qubit state, apply arbitrary local unitary encodings, and transmit one qubit each. However, increasing the local dimension overcomes this obstruction: one shared three-qutrit GHZ state and one transmitted qutrit per player yield a one-shot protocol with total communication $3\log_2 3$. Together with the six-bit classical lower bound, this gives a strict quantum communication advantage. More generally, for every $k\geq 3$, we construct a perfectly correct and perfectly private one-shot protocol for $k$-bit AND using one qudit of dimension at most $k$ per player, and hence at most $k\log_2 k$ qubits in total.

papers.title_en: Search for dark photon in association with charged leptons at electron-positron colliders
papers.abstract_en: The dark photon can serve as a vector portal between the dark sector and the Standard Model via kinetic mixing. In this paper, we investigate the production of an invisible dark photon via the process $e^+ e^- \to \ell^+ \ell^- A'$ with $\ell=e,μ$, at the Circular Electron Positron Collider (CEPC). The production cross sections for the signal process are calculated, and the kinematic distributions for the signal and background processes are analyzed. We further compute the branching ratio for the invisible decay of the dark photon, and explore the discovery potential of dark photons at the CEPC. It is found that dark photons with masses in the range $1~\mathrm{GeV} < M_{A'} < 16~\mathrm{GeV}$ are potentially detectable at the CEPC.

papers.title_en: Controlled PROP: Theory and Applications to Quantum Circuits
papers.abstract_en: Control is a fundamental concept in quantum and reversible computational models. It enables the conditional application of a transformation to a system, depending on the state of another system. We introduce a general framework for diagrammatic reasoning featuring control as a constructor. To this end, we provide an elementary axiomatization of control functors, extending the standard formalism of PROPs to controlled PROPs. As an application, we show that controlled PROPs facilitate diagrammatic reasoning for quantum circuits. In particular, they admit a simple and complete axiomatization involving at most three qubits, whereas in the standard PROP setting, completeness necessarily requires axioms involving arbitrarily many qubits.

papers.title_en: Nonergodicity from Hilbert-Subspace Cloning
papers.abstract_en: We identify a class of nonintegrable quantum many-body systems composed of single Pauli strings that possess an extensive number of noncommuting local conserved quantities and exhibit partial ergodicity breaking due to exponentially degenerate energy spectra. We show that such systems exhibit a novel mechanism, Hilbert-subspace cloning, where the identical chaotic Hamiltonian acts on each of exponentially many disconnected Hilbert subspaces. Although the dynamics within each clone thermalizes, quantum coherence between clones remains protected and detectable by local observables. Consequently, the long-time behavior of local observables is described by a coherence-preserving partial Gibbs ensemble, where the hidden subsystem retains its initial quantum coherence.

papers.title_en: A REST-based Monte Carlo Simulation and Data Analysis Framework for the N$ν$DEx Experiment
papers.abstract_en: The N$ν$DEx experiment is designed to search for neutrinoless double-beta decay ($0νββ$) of $\mathrm{^{82}Se}$ and is planned to be deployed at the China Jinping Underground Laboratory (CJPL). It employs a high-pressure time projection chamber (TPC) filled with $\mathrm{^{82}SeF_6}$ gas and a Topmetal pixelated charge readout system. The high $Q_{ββ}$ value of $\mathrm{^{82}Se}$, together with the track reconstruction capability of a gaseous TPC, provides strong potential for background suppression. In this work, we develop a full simulation and reconstruction framework for the N$ν$DEx experiment based on the REST (Rare Event Searches Toolkit) software framework. To meet the detector-specific requirements of N$ν$DEx, customized simulation processes are implemented to describe the detector geometry, electron drift and diffusion, the Topmetal readout plane, signal formation, and electronics response. These developments enable a complete software description of the detector response from energy deposition to digitized waveforms. A waveform-fitting-based reconstruction method is further applied to the simulated signals to extract the deposited charge and reconstruct the event energy. For simulated signal events, the reconstructed energy resolution reaches a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of less than 1%, satisfying the design requirement of the experiment. The resulting simulation and reconstruction chain provides a basis for future studies of detector response, background rejection, event classification, and optimization of the N$ν$DEx detector design.

papers.title_en: Multiscale Quantum-Classical Simulation of Protein Autoproteolysis in a Million-Atom Membrane Environment
papers.abstract_en: Predicting chemical reactions in biomolecules is challenging because reactive centers are embedded within complex environments that strongly influence their energetics and mechanisms. Here, we present a hybrid quantum-classical workflow that combines molecular dynamics, density functional theory, and correlated wavefunction methods, tightly integrating CPUs, GPUs, and quantum processing units (QPUs) to enable simulations across multiple length and accuracy scales. We apply this approach to ADGRG1 autoproteolysis, a maturation reaction in an adhesion G protein-coupled receptor that has not previously been studied using correlated electronic-structure methods. Our simulations treat a biologically realistic system containing more than one million atoms, including the full-length uncleaved receptor embedded in an endoplasmic-reticulum membrane, while incorporating a 54-qubit IQM quantum processor and up to 1,200 NVIDIA H100 GPUs. These results demonstrate how quantum computers can serve as accelerators within scalable scientific workflows, extending correlated electronic-structure methods to biologically relevant systems.

papers.title_en: Laboratory Characterization of a Ge-CCD Prototype for Future Near-Infrared Astronomical Instrumentation
papers.abstract_en: Germanium charge-coupled devices (Ge-CCDs) extend CCD imaging beyond the silicon cutoff and are candidate detectors for the near-infrared channel of future astronomical instruments, in particular the spectrographs of next-generation wide-field surveys. We report the laboratory characterization at Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL) of a prototype fabricated at MIT Lincoln Laboratory. We describe the cryogenic test system and readout, and present measurements of the output waveform, dark current, readout noise, and X-ray response. The dark current at 94.69 K is $26.12 \pm 0.08$ e$^-$ pixel$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$. Under $^{55}$Fe irradiation without on-chip binning, the charge generated by an X-ray is confined within $2\times2$ pixels, and the Mn K$α$ line has a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of $8.5 \pm 0.1$% for single-pixel events. Since the charge generated by X-rays above about 30 keV spreads over $3\times3$ or more pixels, the CCD was operated with $2\times2$ on-chip binning at higher energies. This yielded FWHMs of $8.4\pm0.4$% at 30.9 keV ($^{133}$Ba, ASCA grades 0, 2, 3, 4, and 6) and $7.45\pm0.04$% at 59.5 keV ($^{241}$Am, all grades). These results establish a baseline for the device and for the BNL test system. Measurements of the temperature dependence, optical response, and charge-transfer performance will connect this baseline to the requirements of near-infrared astronomical instruments.

papers.title_en: Unconditional Quantum PAC Learning Advantage in the Large Error Regime
papers.abstract_en: We establish an unconditional super-polynomial separation between quantum and classical PAC learning of Boolean functions under the uniform distribution in the large error regime. For every advantage $λ(n) = n^{-ω(1)}$, we construct a concept class that a polynomial-time quantum learner learns to agreement $1/2+λ(n)$ with success probability at least $1-1/n^k$. The learner uses only quantum random examples and outputs a polynomial-size deterministic classical circuit. In contrast, no polynomial-time classical learner achieves agreement $1/2 + λ(n)/n^k$ with success probability greater than $1/n^k$, even with membership queries. To achieve this, we develop a nearly-optimal quantum learner that uses quantum random examples to produce a hypothesis achieving a prescribed correlation with an arbitrary Boolean function. The learner generalizes Fourier sampling from parity hypotheses to quadratic hypotheses. While standard Fourier sampling is insensitive to the sign of the correlation, we use interference to bias sampling toward positively correlated hypotheses. This is combined with a careful analysis of the resulting distribution to boost both the learner's success probability and its agreement with the target function. We believe that the resulting quantum learning algorithm might be of independent interest. Finally, although a robust quantum PAC learning advantage holds unconditionally in the large error regime, we note that an analogous separation between quantum and classical learning in the small error regime would imply that $\mathsf{NP} \nsubseteq \mathsf{BPP}$.

papers.title_en: $χ_{c1}(4010)$ as a $D^{*\pm}D^{\mp}$ Molecular State: Mass, Decay Constant, and Width
papers.abstract_en: The charmonium-like state $χ_{c1}(4010)$, recently observed by the LHCb Collaboration in $B^+ \to D^{*\pm}D^{\mp}K^+$ decays, is investigated as an axial-vector $D^{*\pm}D^{\mp}$ molecular state within the QCD sum rule approach. A two-point sum rule incorporating quark, gluon, and mixed vacuum condensates up to dimension $10$ yields the mass and decay constant, $m_{χ_{c1}(4010)} = (4005.89 \pm 47.15)~\text{MeV}$ and $f_{χ_{c1}(4010)} = (2.87 \pm 0.55)\times 10^{-3}~\text{GeV}^{4}$, in agreement with the LHCb measurement. Since this mass lies above the $D^{*\pm}D^{\mp}$ threshold, the strong coupling constants at the $χ_{c1}(4010)D^{*\pm}D^{\mp}$ vertices are extracted from three-point sum rules and used to compute the partial widths of the $D^{*-}D^{+}$ and $D^{*+}D^{-}$ channels. The resulting total width, $Γ_{χ_{c1}(4010)} = (57.64 \pm 9.64)~\text{MeV}$, is compatible with experiment within uncertainties. These results support a $D^{*\pm}D^{\mp}$ molecular interpretation of $χ_{c1}(4010)$ and offer sum-rule predictions for comparison with future measurements at BESIII, LHCb, and Belle~II.

papers.title_en: Exponential-SWAP gate between bosonic motional modes of trapped ions
papers.abstract_en: The exponential-SWAP (eSWAP) gate generates a coherent superposition of identity and SWAP operations, with continuously tunable amplitudes. We experimentally implement this gate between two bosonic motional modes of trapped ions using spin-independent and spin-dependent beam splitter interactions. Measurements of selected slices of the joint characteristic function for distinct input states test the gate and demonstrate continuous control of the identity-SWAP superposition. This implementation provides a tunable interaction for hybrid qubit-bosonic quantum information processing.

papers.title_en: Two-nucleon scattering amplitudes at light quark masses from lattice QCD
papers.abstract_en: We present a lattice-QCD determination of nucleon-nucleon scattering amplitudes at pion masses of $M_π\approx 200$ MeV and $M_π\approx 280$ MeV at a single lattice spacing $a \approx 0.064$ fm on two CLS ensembles. The finite-volume energy spectra are extracted from large Hermitian correlation matrices constructed within the distillation framework using an extensive basis of two-nucleon interpolating operators. To reliably relate the finite-volume spectra to the infinite-volume scattering amplitudes, we employ two recently developed formalisms that explicitly account for the long-range interaction generated by one-pion exchange: the plane-wave quantization condition and the relativistic left-hand-cut formalism. We discuss the quark-mass dependence of the nucleon-nucleon scattering lengths, effective ranges, shape parameters and pole positions. At all pion masses considered, our analysis prefers virtual states in both isospin channels by more than $1σ$. Comparing also results from our previous calculation at $M_π\approx 710$ MeV, we observe that the inverse scattering lengths and binding momenta approach their physical-point phenomenological values monotonically as the pion mass is varied.

papers.title_en: High average flux positron sources driven by a mJ-class laser
papers.abstract_en: We report on the production and characterisation of MeV-scale positron populations driven by a high-repetition-rate, mJ-class laser system. The positrons are generated via a two-step Bethe--Heitler process driven by laser-wakefield-accelerated electron beams propagating through a mm-scale lead converter. At 10 Hz, approximately 1000 positrons in the 0.8--1.7 MeV energy range were measured over 100 accumulated shots. Stable electron acceleration was demonstrated at 10 Hz, 100 Hz, and 1 kHz using approximately 9 mJ of laser energy in the focal spot, indicating the potential for substantially higher average positron fluxes for laser systems operating at kHz repetition rates and energies of 10s of mJ. Such a positron source allows generating sufficiently high average fluxes of MeV-scale positrons while maintaining low positron yields per pulse and narrow temporal distributions, a regime of particular interest for novel applications in material science and fundamental physics. The measured positron yields and spectra are in good agreement with Monte Carlo simulations, supporting the modelling of the positron-production process and magnetic transport system.

papers.title_en: Anisotropic hadronic matter in external magnetic fields
papers.abstract_en: Strong magnetic fields generated in non-central heavy-ion collisions break rotational symmetry and can imprint anisotropy on the produced quantum chromodynamics (QCD) matter. Within a hadron resonance gas framework in the presence of an external magnetic field, we investigate the resulting anisotropy in the equation of state, isothermal compressibility, speed of sound, and conserved-charge fluctuations. We find that the electric-charge susceptibility ratio $χ_4^Q/χ_2^Q$ develops a pronounced directional dependence, driven primarily by the Landau-level structure of charged pions.
